title: First Trimester Nutrition Checklist: Folate, Iron, and Safer Foods
excerpt: Prioritize folic acid, iron-rich foods, hydration, and cooked foods during weeks 1–12
content:
## Introduction to First Trimester Nutrition

During the first trimester, nutrition plays a crucial role in the development of the fetus. Providing adequate nutrients helps prevent birth defects and ensures the health of both mother and baby. In this article, we will explore the essential elements of first trimester nutrition, including folate, iron, and safer foods.

## Folate: A Crucial Nutrient

Folate is a vital nutrient during pregnancy, particularly during the first trimester. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), folate helps prevent birth defects of the neural tube, such as spina bifida and anencephaly. To ensure adequate folate intake, pregnant women should consume folate-rich foods like leafy greens, fruits, and dairy products.

## Iron: An Essential Nutrient

Iron is an essential nutrient during pregnancy, helping produce red blood cells and supply oxygen to the fetus. According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), iron also helps prevent anemia in pregnant women. Iron-rich foods include red meat, poultry, fish, and legumes.

## Safer Foods

During the first trimester, pregnant women should avoid foods that can harm their health and the health of their baby. According to the National Health Service (NHS), foods to avoid include:

* Raw or undercooked foods, such as sushi, sashimi, and raw meat
* Foods containing listeria, such as soft cheeses and cold deli meats
* Foods containing mercury, such as shark and swordfish

## Cooking Foods Thoroughly

To ensure food safety, pregnant women should cook foods thoroughly, especially:

* Meat and poultry: cook to an internal temperature of at least 165°F (74°C)
* Eggs: cook to an internal temperature of at least 165°F (74°C)
* Fish: cook to an internal temperature of at least 145°F (63°C)

## Conclusion

First trimester nutrition is crucial for the development of the fetus. Pregnant women should prioritize folate, iron, and safer foods to ensure the health of both mother and baby. For more information on pregnancy nutrition, visit our [pregnancy meal planner](/planner) page.

## When to Seek Help

If you have any questions or concerns about pregnancy nutrition, consult your healthcare provider or a registered dietitian. They can provide personalized guidance and support to ensure a healthy pregnancy.
